angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 695,700 km at 112.52 pc = 0.08 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 8.8871 +/- 0.0126 mas (same row, RUWE 1.03): 112.52 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1 +/- 0.05 solar radii from Crossfield et al. 2025, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-1691 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025AJ....169...89C/abstract): 695,700 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.03 +/- 0.14 solar masses from Crossfield et al. 2025, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-1691 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025AJ....169...89C/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5759 +/- 187 K from Crossfield et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1691 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025AJ....169...89C/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Crossfield et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1691 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025AJ....169...89C/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-1691.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.451, rounded to two decimals
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-1691 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] 0.052 dex, from Polanski et al. 2024 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024ApJS..272...32P/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-1691 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -0.03058, from Polanski et al. 2024 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024ApJS..272...32P/abstract)
ageSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-1691 (pscomppars): age 6.6 Gyr, from Polanski et al. 2024 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024ApJS..272...32P/abstract)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
